page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.8xlarge is an instance within the High Clock Speed family running under KVM virtualization. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it features 32 dedicated vCPUs backed by Intel Xeon 6149 processors running at a 3.1 GHz clock speed. The server provides 128 GB of system memory, corresponding to 4 GB per vCPU. It does not include hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Networking capabilities on the ecs.hfg5.8xlarge include a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included with the provisioning. The configuration features zero local disk storage, which necessitates the integration of external network-attached block storage for operating system drives and application data persistence.

From an infrastructure cost perspective, the instance maximizes dedicated high-frequency compute cores and memory allocation without bundling local NVMe or SSD storage. This structure reduces overhead for architectures that rely on centralized storage services or stateless execution. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of high-speed local disk I/O, shifting dependency onto network bandwidth limits for data operations.

The configuration is suitable for workloads demanding sustained CPU throughput and moderate memory footprints. Typical deployment scenarios include distributed application servers, large-scale CI/CD build environments, batch processing systems, and web application serving tiers that do not mandate local caching or high-performance local disk storage.

It includes 128 GB of system memory, providing a standard balanced allocation of 4 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a 6 Gbps baseline, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Because the instance comes with no bundled local storage, persistent storage must be attached via network-based block volumes. The instance provides sustained processing capacity without local drive overhead, offering a cost-efficient resource density for centralized infrastructure that leverages remote storage arrays. Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg5.8xlarge fits workloads requiring high CPU clock frequencies alongside substantial memory capacity, including enterprise web serving, compilation and build systems, continuous integration pipelines, and application middleware.
